_doc: KEGG (six headerless TSVs from rest.kegg.jp, restricted licence): no node type and no relationship of its own — KEGG writes rows into the Pathway node and the IN_PATHWAY edge blueprints/reactome.json declares, and declares them identically here because that is how a fragment says 'I write rows into this'. The whole slice is gated on `scripts/build.py --with-kegg` and is off by default: KEGG is not a public database, so a graph carrying it cannot be published, and every row it writes carries source_licence='KEGG-restricted'. Because this fragment adds no key of its own, composing it into a build that did not run prep_kegg.py costs nothing — no empty node type, no audit rule at 0/0. conv_compound_pubchem.tsv is not loaded at all: it returns PubChem Substance ids, not Compound ids, and writing them beside HMDB's pubchem_cid would be wrong and look plausible.
